f-whatnot.claim: Whatnot reports 2026 live sales above $16B, double 2025.
evidence: Whatnot's own trends report projects sales to more than double from $8B.
Over 100 million sports cards sold on the app by October.
f-whatnot.check: Whatnot's annual results or funding announcements.

f-women.claim: No women's sports card beats Caitlin Clark's $660K record by December 31.
evidence: The record is more than 2.5x the largest recent women's sale, Paige Bueckers' $249,750 in August.
Most top women's basketball cards are Panini 1/1s, which appear rarely at auction.
f-women.check: Record-sale coverage from major auction houses and hobby media.

f-pulse.claim: The High-End Pulse for the week of Goldin's Sports Elite close (Nov 14) is $500,000 or higher.
evidence: In the nine weeks logged, the five weeks led by a Heritage, Goldin or Fanatics Premier close had a Pulse of $591K to $2.85M (SI weekly lists).
The two weeks led by eBay and REA sales had a Pulse of $130K and $150K (SI, Sep 7 and Sep 14).
Goldin's Sports Elite auction runs Oct 23 to Nov 14 (Auction Report, Oct 26).
f-pulse.check: The Sports Illustrated Collectibles weekly top 5 list covering Nov 14.

f-psa.claim: PSA's reported backlog falls below 6 million cards by November 30.
evidence: The backlog fell from 8.2M to 7.2M between October 6 and 20.
At that pace it would pass 6M in early to mid-November.
f-psa.check: PSA backlog updates as reported by hobby media.

nba-week1.title: Doncic scores 45 and Warriors rookie Lendeborg 37 on Sunday
nba-week1.why: Big early nights from rookies like Lendeborg and Boozer are what move first-year card prices before the season's flagship releases.
nba-week1.source: GMA News, Nov 2; The Sports Leader (Field Level Media), Oct 31
nba-week1.body: Luka Doncic had 45 points, 15 rebounds and 5 steals as the Lakers beat Toronto 131-125 on November 1, and Golden State rookie Yaxel Lendeborg scored 37 in a 124-112 win over the Clippers. Jayson Tatum scored 32 as Boston beat Orlando 108-97. On Saturday, Victor Wembanyama scored a season-high 43 and Memphis rookie Cameron Boozer a career-high 27.

football-cards.title: Burrow's $81,000 patch auto leads a quiet football card week after a $300K Brady week
football-cards.why: Football's top tier moves with auction calendars, and November's new Topps Chrome Football release is the next big test of demand.
football-cards.source: Sports Illustrated Collectibles, Nov 1; Sports Illustrated Collectibles, Oct 26
football-cards.body: A 2020 National Treasures Joe Burrow rookie patch auto /99 (PSA 10) sold for $81,000 on eBay on October 29, topping a week whose five biggest football sales had a median of $45,000. The week before, all five top sales came in the October 23 Fanatics Premier close, led by a $300,000 2014 Flawless Tom Brady patch auto /10, for a median of $198,000.

mlb-free-agency.title: MLB free agency opens today with four weeks left before the labour deal expires
mlb-free-agency.why: Any star signing has to land in a four-week window, which compresses the usual offseason jersey and card demand into November.
mlb-free-agency.source: MLB Trade Rumors, Nov 1; MLB.com, Nov 1; HERE National Desk, Nov 1
mlb-free-agency.body: Free agents can sign with any club from 5 p.m. ET on November 2, the same day teams must decide on qualifying offers worth $23.15 million; players have until November 17 to answer. By Friday 155 players had become free agents, and San Diego's Michael King declined his option to test the market. The agreement expires December 1, and a lockout would freeze signings and trades.

nwsl-decision.title: Gotham beats Utah 2-0 on Decision Day to win its first NWSL Shield
nwsl-decision.why: Home playoff games for Gotham, San Diego, Kansas City and Washington put the league's biggest gates and national TV windows in four markets.
nwsl-decision.source: AP via ABC News, Nov 1; The Athletic via Yahoo Sports, Nov 1; CBS Sports, Nov 1
nwsl-decision.body: Gotham finished 18-5-7 after goals from Guro Reiten and Jaedyn Shaw, holding off San Diego (18-8-4) for the club's first Shield and home field through the playoffs. Seattle took the last playoff spot with a 1-0 win over Orlando, and Utah's Ashley Sanchez won the Golden Boot with 20 goals, tying the single-season record. Quarterfinals run November 6 to 8: San Diego hosts Utah, Kansas City hosts Angel City, Gotham hosts Seattle and Washington hosts Portland, ahead of the November 21 final.

russia-hockey.title: Court clears Russia to return to international hockey for the first time since 2022
russia-hockey.body: The Court of Arbitration for Sport upheld Russia's appeal of a July IIHF ruling that had kept it out for 2026-27, finding the IIHF's safety concerns were not backed by sufficient evidence, and did not require neutral status. The ruling covers the 2027 men's and women's world championships, the World Juniors and U18 events; the 16-team men's field for Germany in May is already set. The IIHF disagreed but said it will comply.
russia-hockey.why: Russia's return could reshape fields, broadcast interest and sponsor comfort for IIHF events that feature NHL and PWHL players.

psa.title: PSA reopens Value grading at $39.99 while it repays owners of 6,451 stolen cards
psa.body: PSA's Value tier reopened October 29 at $39.99 a card, up from $32.99 before its June pause, and Standard and Priority estimates were cut by 20 business days; the backlog was 7.2 million items on October 20 against a 5 million target. Separately, 6,451 graded items were taken from a FedEx truck outside PSA's Santa Ana facility on October 13; police first estimated the loss at $963,000, over 2,000 are sports cards, and the FBI has joined the case. PSA deactivated the stolen cert numbers, refunded fees and is paying compensation without waiting for the investigation.
psa.why: Cheaper grading pulls lower-value modern cards back into the resale market, while the theft tests how well cert deactivation keeps stolen slabs out of it.
psa.source: Heavy, Oct 28; Sports Collectors Daily; Sports Illustrated Collectibles, Oct 24 and Oct 29

world-series.title: Brewers parade through Milwaukee as a lockout clouds the offseason
world-series.body: Milwaukee held its World Series parade and rally on October 30, with the city expecting about 400,000 people and many school districts closed for the day; Milwaukee beat Tampa Bay 4-1 in Game 5 on October 28 for its first title in 57 years. The Brewers ran a $154.7 million luxury-tax payroll, 19th in MLB, and have $134.4 million committed for 2027, below the owners' proposed $171.2 million floor. Game 3 drew about 8.33 million viewers, the fourth-lowest World Series game ever, while Game 4 reached a preliminary 13.5 million.
world-series.why: A small-market champion keeps most of its roster, but the labour fight decides how long the title glow can be turned into new signings and merchandise.
world-series.source: WPR, Oct 30; MLB.com, Oct 28; Front Office Sports, Oct 29

arsenal-top.title: Arsenal win 1-0 at Liverpool to go top of the Premier League
arsenal-top.why: A title race led by Arsenal and Liverpool keeps two of the most-followed clubs in North America at the centre of Premier League coverage.
arsenal-top.source: VAVEL, Nov 1; This Is Anfield, Nov 1
arsenal-top.body: Kai Havertz scored in the 16th minute from a Declan Rice pass as Arsenal beat Liverpool 1-0 at Anfield on November 1. The win moved Arsenal to the top of the table; they had been second on 21 points before kickoff.

mlb-lockout.title: Manfred says a deal can protect 2027 as a December 1 lockout nears
mlb-lockout.body: Commissioner Rob Manfred says he is confident a deal can come early enough to protect the 2027 season, CNN reported on October 31, while economists including Andrew Zimbalist expect a stoppage could run into spring or early summer. The agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on December 1; owners have proposed a $245.3 million cap and $171.2 million floor, and interim union chief Bruce Meyer calls a cap a nuclear bomb. Free agents can sign with any team from November 2.
mlb-lockout.why: A lockout freezes signings and trades, the moves that drive new jersey and card demand, from the first week of December.
mlb-lockout.source: CNN via Yahoo Sports, Oct 31; Philadelphia Inquirer, Oct 30; AP via WSLS, Oct 29; MLB Trade Rumors, Oct 29

whatnot-ebay.title: eBay GMV rises 15% with record Goldin quarter; Whatnot expects sales to double
whatnot-ebay.body: eBay's third-quarter GMV rose 15% to $23.2 billion; Goldin posted another record GMV quarter, eBay lowered the price thresholds for mandatory trading card authentication in the US and UK, and TCGplayer passed $1 billion in trailing 12-month GMV. eBay is also cutting about 1,000 jobs while shifting resources to collectibles. Whatnot's trends report says its sales should more than double from $8B last year, with over 100 million sports cards sold on the app in 2026.
whatnot-ebay.why: The two largest card marketplaces are both growing card volume and lowering friction for mid-priced sales.
whatnot-ebay.source: eBay Inc. Q3 release, Oct 28; ICv2, Oct 28; Sports Collectors Daily, Oct 20

wnba-finals.title: Valkyries win the first WNBA Finals Game 7 for a title in their second season
wnba-finals.why: A sold-out, record-priced title run in year two gives the league its strongest proof yet that new markets can pay off quickly, with Williams now a Finals MVP name to market.
wnba-finals.source: KRON4, Nov 1; WNBA.com, Oct 31; ESPN, Oct 31; CBS Sports, Nov 1
wnba-finals.body: The Valkyries will celebrate with a parade along San Francisco's Embarcadero at noon on Wednesday, November 4, after beating Atlanta 68-63 at Chase Center on October 31 in the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history. Finals MVP Gabby Williams scored 30, 28 after halftime, a WNBA playoff record for a half, and set Finals records for points (137) and steals (18). The Valkyries have sold out every home game in team history and became the fastest expansion franchise in North American sports to win a title.

sparks-sale.title: ESPN confirms early talks on a Sparks sale at about $700M
sparks-sale.body: ESPN reported that early-stage discussions about selling the Los Angeles Sparks have taken place, backing an earlier Bloomberg report; no deal has been announced. The figure discussed is about $700 million, against Sportico's $400 million valuation. The Sparks went 16-28 last season and missed the playoffs.
sparks-sale.why: A sale near the ask would reset WNBA franchise values and signal how much investors believe women's basketball can grow.
sparks-sale.source: Yahoo Sports, citing ESPN, Oct 27; The Hockey News, citing Bloomberg, Oct 23

lakers-stakes.title: Lakers minority stakes marketed from $250 million each, per report
lakers-stakes.body: Josh Kushner and Bob Iger are offering Lakers minority stakes starting at $250 million apiece as they build their ownership group, Front Office Sports reported on October 30 citing unnamed sources, with a target range of $250 million to $300 million. The pair agreed this summer to buy the team from Mark Walter at a record $12.5 billion valuation; a representative declined to comment.
lakers-stakes.why: Quarter-billion-dollar minority checks would set a new floor for passive stakes in top NBA franchises.

mcdavid-streak.title: McDavid runs his season-opening point streak to 15 games with 39 points
mcdavid-streak.why: A historic month keeps the NHL's top card name in the news while Upper Deck's new-season products hit shelves.
mcdavid-streak.source: AP via ABC News, Nov 1; NHL.com, Nov 1
mcdavid-streak.body: Connor McDavid scored 50 seconds in and added an assist in Edmonton's 4-1 win over the Rangers on November 1, extending his NHL-record season-opening assist streak and his point streak to 15 games. He leads the league with 39 points and is the fastest player in NHL history to 30 assists; the NHL named him its first star of October. The Oilers are 7-0 on the road.

pwhl-growth.title: PWHL lifts minimum salary to $42,000 and rosters to 24 as it grows to 12 teams
pwhl-growth.body: The league and players' association agreed on October 29 to raise the minimum base salary to $42,000 for 2026-27, from about $38,000, rising to $52,500 by 2030-31; rosters grow to 24 and the reserve system ends. With Detroit, Hamilton, Las Vegas and San Jose added, the changes create 104 more roster spots; camps open November 18 and the season starts December 5. The expansion followed a reported $100 million investment from Kilmer Sports Ventures.
pwhl-growth.why: Higher pay and bigger rosters across 12 markets widen the pool of players with a local following, a base for future card demand.
pwhl-growth.source: PWHL, Oct 29; Boston Globe, Oct 29; Sportico, Oct 23

harper-pull.title: Dylan Harper's $2.88M debut patch 1/1 is pulled again in a PrizePicks digital pack
harper-pull.body: A PrizePicks customer pulled Harper's one-of-one debut patch autograph, graded PSA 9 with a 10 autograph, through PrizePicks Packs, which launched on October 21 listing the card's estimated value at $2.88 million. The card sold for $2.88 million including buyer's premium at a September auction. The customer has not said whether they will sell it back through PrizePicks or have it shipped.
harper-pull.why: Fantasy and betting apps are now using seven-figure graded cards as pack prizes, a new channel competing for high-end inventory and casual buyers.
